LayoutLMv3:    Pre-training for Document    AI                   
                                                                                    
                      with Unified  Text and  Image  Masking                        
                                                                                    
               Yupan Huang∗           Tengchao Lv             Lei Cui               
             Sun Yat-sen University Microsoft Research Asia Microsoft Research Asia 
           huangyp28@mail2.sysu.edu.cn tengchaolv@microsoft.com lecu@microsoft.com  
                                                                                    
                           Yutong Lu              Furu Wei                          
                        Sun Yat-sen University Microsoft Research Asia              
                       luyutong@mail.sysu.edu.cn fuwei@microsoft.com                
       ABSTRACT                                                                     
       Self-supervised pre-training techniques have achieved remarkable             
       progress in Document AI. Most multimodal pre-trained models                  
       use a masked language modeling objective to learn bidirectional              
       representations on the text modality, but they differ in pre-training        
       objectives for the image modality. This discrepancy adds difficulty          
       to multimodal representation learning. In this paper, we propose             
       LayoutLMv3 to pre-train multimodal Transformers for Document                 
       AI with unified text and image masking. Additionally, LayoutLMv3             
       is pre-trained with a word-patch alignment objective to learn cross-         
       modal alignment by predicting whether the corresponding image                
       patch of a text word is masked. The simple unified architecture              
       and training objectives make LayoutLMv3 a general-purpose pre-               
       trainedmodelforbothtext-centricandimage-centricDocumentAI (a) Text-centric form under- (b) Image-centric layout anal-
       tasks. Experimental results show that LayoutLMv3 achieves state- standingonFUNSD ysisonPubLayNet
       of-the-art performance not only in text-centric tasks, including             
       form understanding, receipt understanding, and document visual Figure 1: Examples of Document AI Tasks.
       question answering, but also in image-centric tasks such as docu-            
       ment image classification and document layout analysis. The code             
       and models are publicly available at https://aka.ms/layoutlmv3.

       4  RELATED WORK                                                              
                                             Various cross-modal objectives are further developed for vi-
       Multimodalself-supervisedpre-trainingtechniquehasmadea sion and language (VL) alignment learning in multimodal models.
       rapid progress in document intelligence due to its successful applica- Image-text matching is widely used to learn a coarse-grained VL
       tions of document layout and image representation learning [2, 13– alignment [2, 5, 19, 22, 56]. To learn a fine-grained VL alignment,
       15, 17, 25, 28, 31, 32, 40, 41, 50, 52, 54–56]. LayoutLM and following UNITERproposesaword-regionalignmentobjectivebasedonopti-
       works joint layout representation learning by encoding spatial co- mal transports, which calculates the minimum cost of transporting
       ordinates of text [17, 25, 28, 54]. Various works then joint image the contextualized image embeddings to word embeddings [5].
       representationlearningbycombiningCNNswithTransformer[49] ViLT extends this objective to patch-level image embeddings [22].
       self-attention networks. These works either extract CNN grid fea- Unlike natural images, document images imply an explicit fine-
       tures [2, 56] or rely on an object detector to extract region fea- grained alignment relationship between text words and image ar-
       tures [14, 31, 40, 54], which accounts for heavy computation bottle- eas. Using this relationship, UDoc uses contrastive learning and
       neck or requires region supervision. In the field of natural images similarity distillation to align the image and text belonging to the
       vision-and-language pre-training (VLP), research works have seen same area [14]. LayoutLMv2 covers some text lines in raw images
       a shift from region features [5, 47, 48] to grid features [19] to lift and predicts whether each text token is covered [56]. In contrast,
       limitations of pre-defined object classes and region supervision. In- we naturally utilize the masking operations in MIM to construct
       spiredbyvisionTransformer(ViT)[11],therehavealsobeenrecent aligned/unaligned pairs in an effective and unified way.
       efforts in VLP without CNNs to overcome the weakness of CNN.                 
       Still, most rely on separate self-attention networks to learn visual 5 CONCLUSION AND FUTURE WORK
       features; thus, their computational cost is not reduced [12, 29, 57]. In this paper, we present LayoutLMv3 to pre-train the multimodal
       An exception is ViLT, which learns visual features with a light- Transformer for Document AI, which redesigns the model archi-
       weight linear layer and significantly cuts down the model size and tecture and pre-training objectives for LayoutLM. Distinguishing
       running time [22]. Inspired by ViLT, our LayoutLMv3 is the first from the existing multimodal model in Document AI, LayoutLMv3
       multimodal model in Document AI that utilizes image embeddings does not rely on a pre-trained CNN or Faster R-CNN backbone to
       without CNNs.                        extract visual features, significantly saving parameters and elimi-
         Reconstructivepre-trainingobjectivesrevolutionizedrepre- nating region annotations. We use unified text and image masking
       sentationlearning.InNLP research,BERTfirstlyproposed“masked pre-training objectives: masked language modeling, masked image
       language modeling” (MLM) to learn bidirectional representations modeling, and word-patch alignment, to learn multimodal repre-
       andadvancedthestateoftheartsonbroadlanguageunderstanding sentations. Extensive experimental results have demonstrated the
       tasks [9]. In the field of CV, Masked Image Modeling (MIM) aims generality and superiority of LayoutLMv3 for both text-centric and
       to learn rich visual representations via predicting masked content image-centric Document AI tasks with the simple architecture and
       conditioning in visible context. For example, ViT reconstructs the unified objectives. In future research, we will investigate scaling up
       mean color of masked patches, which leads to performance gains pre-trained models so that the models can leverage more training
       in ImageNet classification [11]. BEiT reconstructs visual tokens data to drive SOTA results further. In addition, we will explore few-
       learned by a discrete VAE, achieving competitive results in image shotandzero-shotlearningcapabilitiestofacilitatemorereal-world
       classification and semantic segmentation [3]. DiT extends BEiT to business scenarios in the Document AI industry.
